h: Chocolate, canals and a jungle detour
p: Got a full day in Brum? Mix your adventure golf with a few of the city's other crowd-pleasers. Cadbury World in Bournville is the obvious one for anyone with a sweet tooth, and the village around it, built by the Cadbury family for their workers, is a lovely place for a wander. Closer to the centre, the Library of Birmingham in Centenary Square is worth stepping into just for the building, with its rooftop gardens and views across the city.

Planning the golf bit is easy. A round usually takes about an hour, a little longer if your group is big or likes to stop for photos at every themed hole. Booking a slot means you can plan the rest of the day around it, and turning up ten minutes early gives everyone time to grab a putter and pick a ball colour without a mad scramble.

A few tips for families: let younger children take their shots first so they stay interested, keep the rules simple, and don't be afraid to let the little ones have an extra go now and then. Older kids and teens usually love being trusted with the scorecard. For grown-up groups, a friendly forfeit for the loser keeps the stakes nicely silly.

Afterwards, the Rotunda and the bronze bull outside the Bullring make for a classic Birmingham photo, and Symphony Hall hosts concerts if you're after a more cultured end to the night. Plenty of variety, all within easy reach.
